props.annotationText: Python didn't warn you. Your numbers were strings the whole time.

script: your analysis runs fine, your numbers look reasonable and then six months later

props.description: A cinematic 'type corruption cascade': a DataFrame grid fades in with green dtype badges on each column header (int64, float64). Slowly the 'amount' column badge pulses red and flips to 'object'. A ripple propagates rightward — sum(), mean(), and groupby() output cells flip one by one from correct values (300, 150.0) to wrong concatenated strings ('100200', '100150'). A timestamp watermark materialises at bottom-right reading '6 months later' in muted crimson. Dark background, monospace font, slow eerie glow pulse on corrupted cells.

script: the bug was never in your logic. It was in your data types all along
